title.es: Debate por el parque del barrio

es: Defender una postura en un debate vecinal integrando tesis, argumentos, concesión, refutación enfática y conclusión.

teaching.en: As a resident with a vested interest, I argue that the park should stay open until ten, and I will give two reasons.
teaching.es: Como vecino con un interés personal en juego, sostengo que el parque debería seguir abierto hasta las diez, y daré dos razones.
teaching.explanationEs: Declarar tu interés (a vested interest) es honesto y refuerza la tesis: la tesis va al principio.
segments: As a resident with a vested interest, I argue that the park
should stay open until ten, and I will give two reasons.
teaching.audioText: As a resident with a vested interest, I argue that the park should stay open until ten, and I will give two reasons.

teaching.en: Neighbours can launch a petition; four hundred signatures show that they want to have a say, and the council must listen.
teaching.es: Los vecinos pueden lanzar una recogida de firmas; cuatrocientas firmas muestran que quieren tener voz, y el municipio debe escuchar.
teaching.explanationEs: Launch a petition + have a say: el primer argumento se apoya en evidencia que se puede contar.
segments: Neighbours can launch a petition; four hundred signatures show that they
want to have a say, and the council must listen.
teaching.audioText: Neighbours can launch a petition; four hundred signatures show that they want to have a say, and the council must listen.

teaching.en: Much as I understand the rubbish problem, families need a safe place, and that should not come at the expense of the children.
teaching.es: Por mucho que entienda el problema de la basura, las familias necesitan un lugar seguro, y eso no debe ir a costa de los niños.
teaching.explanationEs: Concesión con Much as + refutación; at the expense of = a costa de, útil para señalar quién pierde.
segments: Much as I understand the rubbish problem, families need a safe place,
and that should not come at the expense of the children.
teaching.audioText: Much as I understand the rubbish problem, families need a safe place, and that should not come at the expense of the children.

teaching.en: Noise is the real sticking point for the houses beside the playground, and I concede that it deserves a serious hearing.
teaching.es: El ruido es el verdadero punto de fricción para las casas junto a la zona de juegos, y reconozco que merece una audiencia seria.
teaching.explanationEs: A sticking point es el obstáculo principal de una negociación; conceder lo que es fuerte da credibilidad.
segments: Noise is the real sticking point for the houses beside the
playground, and I concede that it deserves a serious hearing.
teaching.audioText: Noise is the real sticking point for the houses beside the playground, and I concede that it deserves a serious hearing.

teaching.en: When the plan is put to a vote, the council should hear both sides first, and every resident should be allowed to speak.
teaching.es: Cuando el plan se someta a votación, el municipio debería escuchar primero a ambas partes y dejar hablar a cada vecino.
teaching.explanationEs: Put to a vote (voz pasiva) y hear both sides describen un proceso justo antes de decidir.
segments: When the plan is put to a vote, the council should hear
both sides first, and every resident should be allowed to speak.
teaching.audioText: When the plan is put to a vote, the council should hear both sides first, and every resident should be allowed to speak.

teaching.en: To conclude, the council and the neighbours can reach a compromise: longer hours, a weekend cleaning team and quiet after nine.
teaching.es: Para concluir, el municipio y los vecinos pueden llegar a un acuerdo: más horas, un equipo de limpieza los fines de semana y silencio después de las nueve.
teaching.explanationEs: La conclusión cierra con un acuerdo concreto: reach a compromise = llegar a un término medio.

prompt.es: Localiza la tesis: ¿cuál es la afirmación central del discurso?

choices.text: Many neighbours asked why the speaker opposes the car park.
The old tennis courts should be repaired and reopened, not replaced.
The council deserves thanks for listening to its residents.

feedback.es: La tesis llega tras la pregunta de los vecinos: las pistas deben repararse y reabrirse; el agradecimiento y la pregunta son solo contexto.

hint.es: La tesis es lo que defiende, no lo que agradece ni lo que le han preguntado.

origin.text: Good evening, neighbours. Many of you have asked me why I oppose the car park. I will keep my answer short: the old tennis courts should be repaired and reopened, not replaced. I will give two reasons, but first let me thank the council for listening.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de votar, el municipio prometió escuchar a ambas partes.»

feedback.es: Hear both sides es la colocación para dar voz a las dos posturas antes de decidir.

hint.es: Verbo de percepción auditiva; empieza por h.

origin.text: The car park plan has divided the town. Before anyone casts a vote, the council has promised to ___ both sides of the argument.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por mucho que respete la petición, no puedo apoyarla.»

answer.text: Much as I respect the petition I cannot support it
accepted: Much as I respect the petition I cannot support it
I cannot support it much as I respect the petition

feedback.es: Much as I respect… concede el valor de la petición y la postura propia llega después, sin but; la concesión también puede ir al final.

hint.es: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede la vecina antes de refutar.

choices.text: That the council already manages the rubbish badly.
That the families are the cause of the noise.
That the noise from the playground can be tiring.

feedback.es: «Admittedly, the noise can be tiring» es la concesión; «But what matters is…» abre su refutación.

origin.audio: I have lived beside this playground for twenty years. Admittedly, the noise can be tiring, and I have reservations about the late opening hours. But what matters is that children have somewhere safe to play, and it is the council that should manage the rubbish and the noise, not the families who use the park.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con su paso en la estructura.

pairs: My position is that the car park should go elsewhere
The petition has six hundred signatures
Admittedly, drivers need a place to park
What matters is that the courts stay open to everyone
To conclude, we can reach a compromise

feedback.es: Cada frase ocupa un lugar del debate: la tesis abre, la evidencia apoya, la concesión reconoce, la refutación enfatiza y la conclusión cierra.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere la autora sobre su voto en esta carta a los vecinos?

choices.text: That she has already decided against the plan but will not say so.
That she will follow the majority whatever her own view may be.
That she expects the vote to be cancelled before March.
That she is still unsure and wants to listen before committing.

feedback.es: Dice que no puede prometer nada y que no votará antes de escuchar a los vecinos de ambas posturas: está indecisa y abierta a escuchar.

origin.text: Dear neighbours, thank you for your messages. I cannot promise that the car park will go ahead, and I will not pretend that every objection has an easy answer. All I can say is that a vote will be held in March, and that I shall not vote until I have heard from residents on both sides.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué actitud muestra Mar ante el compromiso de Tom.

choices.text: Open to it, though not ready to accept it on the spot.
Supportive, but only if Tom gives up his Saturday training sessions.
Opposed, rejecting any change to her original proposal for the garden.
Neutral, leaving the whole decision to the club.

feedback.es: Mar no acepta «at once» y quiere escuchar al club, pero admite que media huerta es mejor que nada: apertura con cautela; no pone condiciones a Tom, no rechaza todo cambio ni se desentiende.

origin.audio: Sol chaired the meeting about the old tennis courts. Mar spoke first and put forward her thesis: the courts should become a community garden. Her evidence was a petition with five hundred signatures. Tom, who has a vested interest because he trains there on Saturdays, conceded that a garden would look lovely, but what matters to him is that teenagers have a place to play. He proposed a compromise: half the land for vegetables, half for the courts. Mar did not accept at once. She said she would need to hear both sides of the club first, although she admitted that half a garden was better than none. Sol then put the idea to a vote.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿por qué menciona el narrador que Tom tiene «a vested interest»?

choices.text: To show that Tom has the legal power to stop the garden.
To suggest that his view may reflect his own use of the courts.
To explain why Tom collected the five hundred signatures.
To hint that Mar herself has no interest in the old courts at all.

feedback.es: El narrador explica que Tom entrena allí los sábados: su postura puede estar influida por su propio interés; no colecta firmas ni tiene poder legal.

origin.audio: Sol chaired the meeting about the old tennis courts. Mar spoke first and put forward her thesis: the courts should become a community garden. Her evidence was a petition with five hundred signatures. Tom, who has a vested interest because he trains there on Saturdays, conceded that a garden would look lovely, but what matters to him is that teenagers have a place to play. He proposed a compromise: half the land for vegetables, half for the courts. Mar did not accept at once. She said she would need to hear both sides of the club first, although she admitted that half a garden was better than none. Sol then put the idea to a vote.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos decidieron lanzar una recogida de firmas.»

feedback.es: Launch a petition es la colocación habitual para iniciar una recogida de firmas; start o organise también encajan.

origin.text: Unhappy with the plan, the neighbours decided to ___ a petition that any resident could sign. Within a week it had four hundred signatures, and the council had to reply.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el debate del parque, de la tesis a la conclusión.

answer.text: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want a say and want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I have reservations about the late hours for the people who live next to the park. Much as I understand their tiredness, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it, and that should not come at the expense of the children. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, we can reach a compromise: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine, and the council puts the plan to a vote.

In my view, the park should remain open until ten at night. First, the petition has 400 signatures, so the residents clearly want longer hours and a say in the decision. Second, there is no other playground nearby, and families need somewhere safe to go after work. Much as I understand the noise problem, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. I concede that there is some rubbish at weekends; nevertheless, it is the council that must keep the park clean, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing earlier would only move the problem somewhere else, and it would happen at the expense of the children. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park stays open until ten, with silence after nine, and the plan goes to a vote.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención tiene tesis, dos argumentos con evidencia, concesión, refutación enfática y una conclusión con acuerdo.

origin.text: Debate vecinal: ¿debe el parque abrir hasta las diez de la noche? Defiendes que sí. Escribe unas 210–270 palabras con: tesis; dos argumentos (una petición con 400 firmas y que no hay otra zona de juegos); una concesión sobre el ruido y la basura; una refutación con frase hendida; y una conclusión con un acuerdo (silencio desde las nueve).

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el comunicado del municipio?

choices.text: That the council has quietly decided to reject the petition.
That the eleven letters will outweigh the signed petition.
That the council means to delay a decision without backing either side.
That residents will be able to vote on the park hours in spring.

feedback.es: «Take every view into account» y «no decision before the spring» sugieren aplazar sin comprometerse; por eso un vecino lo llama «a polite way of doing nothing».

origin.text: The council has received 412 signatures calling for longer park hours and eleven letters opposing them. Officials say they will take every view into account, and that no decision will be made before the spring. Residents who hoped for a quick answer were not reassured; one of them called the statement a polite way of doing nothing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es el municipio quien debe ofrecer un lugar seguro.»

answer.text: It is the council that must provide a safe place

feedback.es: It is + elemento + that: la hendida pone al municipio como responsable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aún pueden llegar a un acuerdo antes de la votación.»

feedback.es: Reach a compromise es la colocación habitual; find o strike a compromise también son naturales.

origin.text: The two sides have little in common, but they may still ___ a compromise before the vote takes place next month.
